name: DMIN
description: DMIN returns the smallest numeric value in a specified field of the database records that match the given criteria.
tldr: Returns the minimum value in a database column for rows that meet the criteria.

parameters.name: database
parameters.description: The range containing the database, including the header row as the first row.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: The column to inspect, given as the column label in quotes (e.g. "Yield") or its 1-based column index.

parameters.name: criteria
parameters.description: The range with a header row matching database column names and one or more condition rows; only matching records are considered.

basicExample.description: Find the lowest Yield among apple trees taller than 10
basicExample.explanation: The criteria A9:B10 (Tree=Apple, Height>10) matches two rows with Yield 14 and 10; the smallest is 10.

advancedExamples.title: Minimum Profit among matching trees
advancedExamples.description: Use the same criteria but a different field to find the lowest Profit.
advancedExamples.explanation: The two matching rows have Profit 105 and 75, so the minimum is 75.

advancedExamples.title: Minimum across a single condition
advancedExamples.scenario: Lowest Yield for any apple tree
advancedExamples.description: Criteria A9:A10 is Tree=Apple across all three apple rows.
advancedExamples.explanation: Apple yields are 14, 10, and 6; the minimum is 6.

howItWorks: DMIN filters the database to rows matching the criteria, then returns the smallest numeric value found in the specified field column of those rows. If no records match, DMIN returns 0.

howToSteps.name: Set up the database
howToSteps.text: Enter your table with a header row, e.g. A1:E7 with Tree, Height, Age, Yield, Profit.

howToSteps.name: Set up criteria
howToSteps.text: Place criteria headers and values in a separate range, e.g. A9:B10.

limitations: Considers only numeric values in the field; text is ignored.
If no records match, DMIN returns 0 rather than an error.
Criteria header labels must exactly match database headers.

commonErrors.cause: No rows matched the criteria, so there is no value to minimize.
commonErrors.fix: Check that the criteria headers and conditions match the database.

commonErrors.cause: The field was an unquoted column name.
commonErrors.fix: Wrap the field name in quotes, e.g. "Yield", or use the column index.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DMIN works identically in Google Sheets with the same arguments and behavior.

faq.question: What does DMIN return if nothing matches?
Does DMIN ignore text in the field?
faq.answer: Yes. Only numeric values in matching rows are considered for the minimum.

faq.question: How is DMIN different from MINIFS?
faq.answer: DMIN filters a multi-column database by a full criteria range, while MINIFS applies multiple single-range conditions.
